vrstilni_peti.predictableError: reusing the cardinal — 'pet nadstropje' instead of the ordinal 'peto nadstropje'

vrstilni_sesti.predictableError: in writing Slovene marks an ordinal with a full stop — '6. nadstropje' is read 'šesto nadstropje', not 'šest'

vrstilni_sedmi.predictableError: the -e- of 'sedem' drops in the ordinal — 'sedmi', not 'sedemi'

vrstilni_osmi.predictableError: the -e- of 'osem' drops in the ordinal — 'osmi', not 'osemi'

vrstilni_deveti.predictableError: after 'v' the ordinal goes locative — 'v devetem razredu', not 'v deveti razred'

vrstilni_deseti.predictableError: a calendar date puts the ordinal in the genitive — 'desetega maja', not nominative 'deseti maj'

vrstilni_dvanajsti.predictableError: mixing it with the clock — twelve o'clock is 'ob dvanajstih', while 'dvanajsti' is the twelfth (floor, date, grade)

pritlicje.predictableError: calling it 'prvo nadstropje' on the English model — in Slovenia the ground floor is 'pritličje' and 'prvo nadstropje' is one flight up; location is locative 'v pritličju'

nadstropje.predictableError: 'v prvem nadstropju' — locative after 'v', with the ordinal agreeing in the neuter; not 'v prvo nadstropje'

razred.predictableError: 'v tretjem razredu' (locative) for which grade you are in; a university year is 'letnik', not 'razred'

ponedeljek.predictableError: 'on Monday' is 'v ponedeljek' — 'v' + ACCUSATIVE; a masculine day looks unchanged because its accusative is identical to the nominative. Not 'na ponedeljek' on the English 'on' model.

torek.predictableError: the fleeting -e- drops when it declines — 'od torka do četrtka', not 'od toreka'

sreda.predictableError: 'v' + accusative — 'v sredo', not 'v sreda'; the feminine -o is where the case becomes visible.

cetrtek.predictableError: confusing 'četrtek' (Thursday) with 'četrt' (a quarter of an hour); 'on Thursday' is 'v četrtek'

petek.predictableError: confusing 'petek' (Friday) with 'pet' (five); the genitive in a range is 'do petka'

sobota.predictableError: 'v' + accusative 'v soboto' for 'on Saturday'; genitive 'do sobote' in a range.

nedelja.predictableError: 'v' + accusative 'v nedeljo'; and it is the LAST day of the Slovene week, listed after 'sobota', not the first.

januar.predictableError: 'in January' is the bare genitive 'januarja' (or 'v januarju') — never 'v januar'

februar.predictableError: English-shaped 'februari'; it is 'februar', and 'in February' is 'februarja'

marec.predictableError: the fleeting -e- drops — the genitive is 'marca' ('marca 2026'), not 'mareca'

april.predictableError: 'in April' is 'aprila'; beginners add a preposition and say 'v april'

maj.predictableError: 'in May' is 'maja' — the same form as the girl's name Maja, which throws learners off; it is still the plain genitive

junij.predictableError: confusing it by ear with 'julij' (July); genitive 'junija' loses nothing

julij.predictableError: confusing it by ear with 'junij' (June) — the one letter is the whole difference

avgust.predictableError: spelt and said with a v — 'avgust', not the English-looking 'august'

september.predictableError: the fleeting -e- drops — 'septembra' for 'in September', not 'septemberja'

december.predictableError: the fleeting -e- drops — 'decembra', not 'decemberja'; and month names are lowercase in Slovene

teden.predictableError: 'this week' is the bare 'ta teden' with no preposition; and the fleeting -e- drops in the plural — 'pet tednov', not 'pet tedenov'

mesec.predictableError: 'for a month' / 'in a month' is 'en mesec' / 'čez en mesec'; and 'mesec' also means moon — the month is meant only in a time phrase

leto.predictableError: the genitive plural is irregular 'let' — 'pet let', not 'pet letov'; dual is 'dve leti'

vikend.predictableError: 'over the weekend' is 'čez vikend' or 'za vikend' — not 'na vikend' on the English 'on' model

od_do.predictableError: BOTH 'od' and 'do' take the genitive — 'od ponedeljka do petka', 'od osmih do štirih' — not nominative 'od ponedeljek do petek'

pol_gen.predictableError: Slovene counts forward to the COMING hour, so 'pol sedmih' is 6:30, not 7:30; the hour goes genitive plural ('pol sedmih', 'pol desetih').

cetrt.predictableError: counting backwards like English — 'četrt na sedem' is 6:15 and 'tri četrt na sedem' is 6:45, both pointing at the COMING hour; in speech you'll also hear 'petnajst čez šest' and 'petnajst do sedmih'.

minuta.predictableError: genitive plural from five up — 'pet minut', not 'pet minute'; the dual is 'dve minuti'

tocno.predictableError: putting it after the time on the English 'five o'clock sharp' model — Slovene says 'točno ob petih', with 'točno' in front

zamuda.predictableError: a person is late with the verb — 'zamujam' — while 'zamuda' is the delay itself: 'Vlak ima deset minut zamude.' (genitive after the number).

in.predictableError: leaving a bare pause between two clauses instead of joining them with 'in' — the speaking rubric listens for it; note that inside a number 'in' is written as one word ('enaindvajset')

potem.predictableError: 'potem' sequences what comes next ('Najprej ..., potem ...'); it is not the cause word — that is 'ker' — nor the result word 'zato'.

ampak.predictableError: putting it at the end of the clause like English 'though', or reaching for 'pa' — 'ampak' opens the contrasting clause after a comma: 'Rad bi kavo, ampak nimam denarja.'

zato.predictableError: swapping it with 'ker' — 'ker' gives the cause, 'zato' the result ('Dežuje, zato ostanem doma'); and it is not the question word 'zakaj'

ali_or.predictableError: the same word also opens a yes/no question; between two nouns it is plainly 'or' — 'Kavo ali čaj?', and both options take the same case.

to_je.predictableError: agreeing 'to' with the noun ('Ta je knjiga', 'Ta je moja žena') — 'to' stays the invariable neuter, and two or more things take 'To so ___.'

na_sliki.gloss: In the picture there is / are ___.
na_sliki.predictableError: 'na slika' — after 'na' for a location it is the locative 'na sliki'; and the verb switches to 'so' for two or more ('Na sliki so trije ljudje.')

tukaj_je.gloss: ___ is here / here's where ___ is (pointing something out)
tukaj_je.predictableError: this is the LOCATIONAL 'here is' — pointing at where a thing stands ('Tukaj je banka.'). Handing something over is 'Izvolite', not 'Tukaj je'.

moski.predictableError: the nominative plural is IDENTICAL to the singular — 'en moški' / 'trije moški' — so only the numeral tells you how many; and the same word is also the adjective 'male'

zenska.predictableError: confusing 'ženska' (a woman) with 'žena' (a wife); the accusative is 'žensko'

otrok.predictableError: the plural is irregular — 'dva otroka', 'trije otroci', and the genitive plural is the bare 'pet otrok'; never 'otroki'

fant.predictableError: 'moj fant' means 'my boyfriend', not 'my boy' — for a son say 'sin'; animate, so the accusative is 'fanta'

dekle.predictableError: 'dekle' is neuter despite meaning a female — 'lepo dekle', 'to dekle', 'mlado dekle', never 'lepa dekle'

ljudje.predictableError: after a number from five up it goes genitive plural 'ljudi' — 'pet ljudi', 'koliko ljudi' — while 3 and 4 take the masculine 'trije/štirje ljudje'

oseba.predictableError: 'oseba' is always feminine even about a man — 'ena oseba', 'dve osebi', 'pet oseb'; never 'dva oseba'

druzina.predictableError: 'družina' is feminine — 'moja družina je velika' — and it takes the accusative as an object: 'Imam veliko družino.' Beware 'družina' is the family unit; relatives more broadly are 'sorodniki'.

mlad.predictableError: the adjective agrees with what it describes — 'mlad moški', 'mlada ženska', 'mlado dekle' — English speakers leave it frozen as 'mlad'

star.gloss: old (of a person or a thing)
star.predictableError: the same word does double duty — 'star moški' (an old man) and 'Star sem 30 let' (age); as a describing word it must agree: 'stara ženska', 'staro mesto'

visok.gloss: tall (of a person); high (of a thing)
visok.predictableError: one word covers both English 'tall' and 'high', and it agrees — 'visoka ženska', 'visoko drevo'

majhen.predictableError: the fleeting -e- drops the moment it inflects — 'majhna soba', 'majhno stanovanje', 'majhni otroci' — not 'majhena'

vesel.predictableError: agreement — 'vesela ženska', 'veseli otroci'; 'vesel' is the cheer you can see in a picture, while 'srečen' is the deeper 'fortunate/happy'

lep.predictableError: 'lep' agrees as an adjective ('lepa hiša', 'lepo mesto'), while 'lepo' as a standalone is the adverb ('lepo poje')

velik.predictableError: agreement — 'velika hiša', 'veliko stanovanje'; and beware that neuter-looking 'veliko' separately means 'a lot of' + genitive ('veliko ljudi')

dela_3sg.predictableError: one form covers both English tenses — 'dela' is 'he works' and 'he is working', so there is no auxiliary to add; the slip is answering 'Kaj dela?' with the 1sg 'delam', or reaching for 'deluje', which is 'functions/operates', not 'works for a living'

govori_3sg.predictableError: 'talking WITH someone' is 'z' + instrumental — 'govori z ženo', not 'govori s žena'; the language is an adverb ('govori slovensko')

je_3sg.gloss: to eat — 3sg 'je' (he/she eats), identical in form to 'je' = is
je_3sg.predictableError: the 3sg 'je' is spelt exactly like 'je' = is — only the accusative object separates them ('Moški je sendvič.' = the man is EATING a sandwich; in careful writing you will see it marked 'jé'). The 3pl is the irregular 'jedo'.

pije_3sg.predictableError: the drink goes accusative — 'pije kavo', not 'pije kava'; 3pl is 'pijejo'

kupuje_3sg.predictableError: for an action in progress you need the imperfective 'kupuje'; the perfective 'kupi' means 'buys/will buy' the once, so a picture is always 'kupuje'

caka_3sg.predictableError: 'waiting for' is 'na' + accusative or nothing at all — 'čaka na avtobus' / 'čaka avtobus' — never the English-shaped 'čaka za avtobus'

sedi_3sg.predictableError: 'sedi' is the state of sitting; sitting DOWN is the different verb 'usede se'. Where they sit is locative — 'sedi na klopi', 'sedi v kavarni'

stoji_3sg.predictableError: Slovene has two verbs spelt 'stati' — this one gives 'stoji' (stands), the other gives 'stane' (costs); they are not forms of one word

kuha_3sg.predictableError: the dish goes accusative — 'kuha juho'; and note 'kuha kavo' is how Slovene says 'makes coffee'

gleda_3sg.predictableError: no preposition and an accusative object — 'gleda televizijo', 'gleda otroke', not 'gleda na televizijo'

pogovarjata_se.gloss: the two of them are talking / chatting (to each other) — dual
pogovarjata_se.predictableError: exactly two people take the DUAL 'pogovarjata se'; three or more take 'pogovarjajo se'. The reflexive 'se' can never be dropped, and it never comes first — it is a second-position clitic ('Pogovarjata se.', 'Dva moška se pogovarjata.').

trije_stirje.gloss: three / four people (the masculine-plural numeral forms)
trije_stirje.predictableError: masculine 3 and 4 have their own shapes — 'trije ljudje', 'štirje moški' — not the neuter/feminine 'tri'/'štiri'; from five up it flips to the genitive plural, 'pet ljudi'

dve_osebi.predictableError: the dual, not the plural — 'dve osebi', never 'dve osebe'; and 'oseba' is feminine, so it is 'dve', never 'dva'

banka.predictableError: being there is locative 'v banki'; going there is accusative 'v banko' — the -i/-o ending is the whole difference

posta.predictableError: the post office takes 'na', not 'v' — 'na pošti' (at), 'na pošto' (to)

trgovina.predictableError: 'v trgovini' (in the shop) vs 'v trgovino' (to the shop); the activity of shopping is the separate word 'nakupovanje'

lekarna.predictableError: 'v lekarni' / 'v lekarno'; a 'drogerija' is a toiletries shop and does not dispense medicine

kino.predictableError: it is masculine even though it ends in -o — 'v kino' (to the cinema), 'v kinu' (at the cinema); not neuter 'v kinem'

trznica.predictableError: the market takes 'na' — 'na tržnici' (at), 'na tržnico' (to) — never 'v tržnici'

hotel.predictableError: 'v hotelu' (at the hotel, locative) vs 'v hotel' (to the hotel); inanimate, so the accusative equals the nominative

postaja.predictableError: it takes 'na' — 'na postaji' (at the stop), 'na postajo' (to the stop); and 'do postaje' is genitive after 'do'

sola.predictableError: 'v šoli' (at school) vs 'v šolo' (to school); Slovene uses no article, so it is just 'grem v šolo'

v_na_lok.gloss: in / at ___ — where something IS: locative ('v trgovini', 'na pošti')
v_na_lok.predictableError: location takes the LOCATIVE ('v trgovini', 'na pošti'), while motion towards takes the accusative ('grem v trgovino') — and which preposition is lexical: 'v banki / v trgovini / v šoli' but 'na pošti / na tržnici / na postaji'

doma.predictableError: 'doma' already means 'at home' — no preposition ('Sem doma', never 'v doma'); going home is the separate word 'domov'

zunaj.predictableError: 'zunaj' is being outside; going out is 'ven' — 'Otroci so zunaj' vs 'Gremo ven'

mesto.predictableError: 'v mestu' (in town) — locative, neuter; and watch the second sense, 'prosto mesto' is a free SPOT, not a free city

ulica.predictableError: an address takes 'na' + locative and the street name is an adjective that agrees — 'na Slovenski ulici', not 'na Slovenska ulica'

stanovanje.predictableError: neuter locative after 'v' — 'Živim v stanovanju', not 'v stanovanji' or 'v stanovanje'

hisa.predictableError: 'v hiši' (in the house); a 'hiša' is a whole detached house — the flat you rent in a building is 'stanovanje', not 'hiša'

soba.predictableError: 'v sobi' (locative); 'soba' alone is just 'a room' — a living room is 'dnevna soba' and a bedroom is 'spalnica'

kopalnica.predictableError: 'kopalnica' is where you wash; the toilet is 'stranišče' and in Slovene flats it is often a separate room — asking for the 'kopalnica' in a bar gets you a puzzled look

blok.predictableError: 'v bloku' (locative) is the building; your own flat inside it is still 'stanovanje' — the two are not interchangeable

drzava_slovenija.predictableError: the bare nominative only works as a subject — it is 'v Sloveniji' (locative) for 'in Slovenia' and 'iz Slovenije' (genitive) for 'from Slovenia'

drzava_anglija.predictableError: genitive after 'iz' — 'Sem iz Anglije', not 'iz Anglija'; and 'Anglija' is England only, the UK is 'Velika Britanija'

drzava_amerika.predictableError: 'iz Amerike' (genitive), 'v Ameriki' (locative); everyday Slovene says 'Amerika' where the official name is 'Združene države'

drzava_nemcija.predictableError: 'iz Nemčije' / 'v Nemčiji'; the nationality is 'Nemec / Nemka' and the language is the adverb 'nemško'

drzava_italija.predictableError: 'iz Italije' / 'v Italiji'; the nationality is 'Italijan / Italijanka'

drzava_hrvaska.predictableError: Croatia takes 'na', not 'v' — 'na Hrvaškem' (in Croatia), 'na Hrvaško' (to Croatia), 's Hrvaške' (from Croatia); it declines like an adjective

drzava_avstrija.predictableError: spelt with a v — 'Avstrija' — and not to be confused with 'Avstralija'; 'iz Avstrije' / 'v Avstriji'

sem_anglez.predictableError: the nationality is a capitalised NOUN with its own feminine form — a woman says 'Angležinja' — and it takes no preposition: 'Sem Anglež' but 'Sem iz Anglije'

rad_verb.predictableError: 'rad' takes a FINITE verb, not an infinitive — 'Rad berem', 'Rada kuham', never 'rad brati'; and this is not 'rad bi', which is a one-off wish ('I'd like'), so dropping or adding 'bi' changes the meaning entirely

hobi.predictableError: the plural is 'hobiji' ('moji hobiji so …'); in speech Slovenes far more often open with 'V prostem času …' than with 'Moj hobi je …'

sport.predictableError: 'doing sport' is the reflexive verb + instrumental — 'ukvarjam se s športom' — never the calque 'delam šport'

glasba.predictableError: accusative object — 'poslušam glasbo', not 'poslušam glasba'; 'muzika' is a loose colloquialism, 'glasba' is the word

branje.predictableError: the natural spoken line is the verb — 'Rad berem' — with the noun 'branje' kept for listing; and it is neuter ('branje me veseli')

kuhanje.predictableError: same as 'branje' — say 'Rada kuham' rather than 'Moj hobi je kuhanje'; the noun is neuter

sprehod.predictableError: 'go for a walk' is 'grem na sprehod' — 'na' + accusative — not 'za sprehod' or 'v sprehod'

zena.predictableError: 'žena' is specifically a WIFE — a woman in general is 'ženska'; accusative 'ženo', instrumental 'z ženo'

moz.predictableError: 'mož' is specifically a HUSBAND — a man in general is 'moški'; it is animate, so the accusative is 'moža' ('imam moža')

sin.predictableError: animate masculine — 'imam sina', not 'imam sin'; the plural is the irregular 'sinovi'

hci.predictableError: it declines off a different stem — accusative 'hčer', plural 'hčere' — and in everyday Ljubljana speech people mostly just say 'hčerka'

brat.predictableError: animate — 'imam brata', not 'imam brat'; the plural is the irregular 'bratje'

sestra.predictableError: accusative 'sestro'; the counted forms are 'dve sestri' (dual) and the genitive plural 'pet sester'

porocen_sem.predictableError: gender — a man says 'poročen', a woman 'poročena'; 'married TO someone' is 'poročen z' + instrumental, and the opposite is 'samski / samska'

stevilo_enote_desetice.gloss: compound numerals 21–99: the UNIT first, then -in-, then the whole tens word, all as one word — shown here on the 20s and 30s, and the same rule runs to 99 (enaindvajset 21, petintrideset 35, devetindevetdeset 99)
stevilo_enote_desetice.predictableError: English order — saying the tens first ('dvajset ena'). Slovene puts the UNIT first and glues it on with -in- to the full tens word, all as ONE written word: 21 = ena+in+dvajset 'enaindvajset', 35 'petintrideset', 45 'petinštirideset', 99 'devetindevetdeset'.

stevilo_enaindvajset.predictableError: the Listening paper's three-way trap — 'dvanajst' (12), 'enaindvajset' (21), 'trideset' (30); 21 is built on 'dvajset', so its ending sounds nothing like the teen's '-najst'

konec_tedna.predictableError: 'konec' takes the GENITIVE — 'konec tedna', never 'konec teden'; 'at the weekend' is 'ob koncu tedna' (locative), and this is the form you meet on signs and in print, not in the bar

boli_me.predictableError: the body part is the SUBJECT and stays nominative — 'Boli me glava', never 'boli me glavo'; the person is the accusative clitic 'me', not a possessive ('moja glava boli'). Two or more parts flip the verb: 'Bolijo me noge.'

glava.predictableError: in 'Boli me glava' it is the subject in the nominative — the slip is the accusative 'boli me glavo' on the English 'my head' model

trebuh.predictableError: 'trebuh' is the belly you point at; 'želodec' is the stomach organ — for a stomach ache you say 'Boli me trebuh'

grlo.predictableError: it is neuter — 'vneto grlo' (a sore throat), not 'vnet grlo'

zob.predictableError: the nominative plural is irregular 'zobje' (not 'zobi'), and two or more flip the verb — 'Bolijo me zobje'; one aching tooth is just 'Boli me zob'

slabo_mi_je.predictableError: the person is the dative clitic 'mi' — 'Slabo mi je', not 'Sem slab'; and it means nauseous/faint, not 'I feel bad' in general, which is 'Slabo se počutim'

vrocina.predictableError: 'I have a fever' takes the accusative — 'Imam vročino', not 'imam vročina'

prehlad.predictableError: Slovenes say 'Prehlajen sem. / Prehlajena sem.' — participle first, since 'sem' is a second-position clitic; the calque 'Imam prehlad.' is said but noticeably less idiomatic. A cold is not 'gripa' (flu).

zdravnik.predictableError: 'to the doctor' is 'k' + DATIVE — 'grem k zdravniku', not 'k zdravnik'

recept.predictableError: the same word means 'recipe' — at the pharmacy the distinction is 'na recept' (on prescription) vs 'brez recepta' (over the counter)

tableta.predictableError: you normally ask in the plural — 'tablete proti bolečinam'; accusative singular is 'tableto' and 'pet tablet' is the genitive plural

vlak.predictableError: 'by train' is 'z' + INSTRUMENTAL — 'z vlakom', not 'z vlak'; and 'na vlak' (boarding) vs 'na vlaku' (aboard)

vozovnica.predictableError: accusative 'vozovnico' — 'Eno vozovnico, prosim'; at a ticket window locals very often just say 'karta' ('Eno karto do Maribora, prosim'), and a cinema or museum ticket is 'vstopnica'

peron.predictableError: 'on platform 2' is the locative 'na drugem peronu'; note Slovenian station announcements usually say 'tir' (track), not 'peron'

odhod.predictableError: 'odhod' (od- = away) is departure and 'prihod' (pri- = towards) is arrival — the prefix is the whole difference on a board

prihod.predictableError: mirror of 'odhod' — beginners read the two off a board by the shared '-hod' and pick the wrong column

prtljaga.predictableError: it is a feminine SINGULAR mass noun covering all your bags — 'moja prtljaga je težka', not an English-style plural; 'prtljage' is the genitive singular ('nimam prtljage'), not 'bags'

taksi.predictableError: the stem gains a -j- when it declines — 's taksijem' (by taxi), 'v taksiju' — not 'z taksi'

avto.predictableError: masculine even though it ends in -o, like 'kino' — 'z avtom', 'v avtu'; beginners decline it as a neuter

z_s_instr.gloss: by ___ / with ___ — the means: 'z avtom', 'z vlakom', 's taksijem'
z_s_instr.predictableError: the means takes the INSTRUMENTAL ('z avtom', not 'z avto'), and the preposition is 's' before a voiceless consonant ('s taksijem', 's kartico') but 'z' elsewhere

rezervacija.predictableError: accusative 'rezervacijo' — 'Imam rezervacijo'; it is the noun, and it cannot stand in for the verb 'rezervirati'

kljuc.predictableError: 'the room key' is 'ključ od sobe' — genitive after 'od'; and it is inanimate, so the accusative equals the nominative ('dobim ključ')

za_dve_noci.predictableError: 'noč' is feminine and its dual is 'dve noči' — not 'dva noči' or 'dve noč'

odprto.predictableError: the sign is the neuter 'Odprto'; describing the shop the adjective agrees — 'trgovina je odprta' — and asking a person is 'Ali ste odprti?'

zaprto.predictableError: the sign is the neuter 'Zaprto'; with a noun it agrees — 'trgovina je zaprta', 'muzej je zaprt'

prepovedano.predictableError: on its own the sign is the neuter 'Prepovedano', but attached to a noun it agrees — 'Vstop prepovedan', 'Kajenje prepovedano'

vstop.predictableError: 'vstop' is entry as an act — the doorway itself is 'vhod'; the sign reads 'Vstop prepovedan', 'Vstop prost'

izhod.predictableError: confusing 'izhod' (the door out) with 'odhod' (a departure time); the emergency exit is 'izhod v sili'

pozor.predictableError: the printed word is the bare noun 'Pozor!'; the spoken warning to a person is the verb 'Pazi!' / 'Pazite!'

informacije.predictableError: the desk is always the plural 'Informacije'; a single piece of information is the singular 'informacija' ('Hvala za informacijo.')

odpiralni_cas.gloss: opening hours (of a shop, a museum)
odpiralni_cas.predictableError: the phrase is masculine — 'kakšen je odpiralni čas', not 'kakšni'; 'odpiralni čas' is the shop-door wording, and you will just as often see 'delovni čas' on the same door

popust.predictableError: a percentage takes the GENITIVE — '20 % popusta', 'popust na vse' — not '20 % popust'

cena.predictableError: 'cena' is the printed price; across a counter Slovenes ask 'Koliko stane?', not the stiff 'Kakšna je cena?'

delo.predictableError: 'delo' is work in general ('iščem delo'); the paid post you actually hold is 'služba' ('imam novo službo') — English 'job' maps to both

iscemo.gloss: We are looking for ___. (the job-ad frame)
iscemo.predictableError: the object goes accusative, and an animate masculine takes -a — 'Iščemo natakarja', not 'Iščemo natakar'

oddam.gloss: For rent / to let: I let out ___. (as written by a private owner; an agency writes 'Oddamo')
oddam.predictableError: English 'rent' goes both ways — 'oddam' is the owner letting it out ('Oddam stanovanje'), while renting FROM someone is 'najamem'; and the next card along reading 'PRODAM' is for SALE, not for rent.

tecaj.predictableError: 'a Slovene course' is the genitive 'tečaj slovenščine', and you attend it with 'na' + accusative — 'hodim na tečaj'; the same word also means exchange rate

prijava.predictableError: 'prijava' is the noun on the notice ('Prijave zbiramo do 10. septembra'); signing yourself up is the verb 'prijavim se' — the noun cannot stand in for it

vceraj_sem.gloss: Yesterday I ___ed — the past tense: the -l participle + 'sem'
vceraj_sem.predictableError: the participle agrees with the SPEAKER'S gender — a man says 'Včeraj sem bil', a woman 'Včeraj sem bila' — and 'sem' alone carries the past; there is no second auxiliary to add

bil_sem.sl: Bil sem doma. / Bila sem doma.
bil_sem.predictableError: the past of 'biti' is the participle 'bil/bila' PLUS 'sem' — dropping 'sem' ('jaz bil doma') leaves no tense at all

sel_sem.predictableError: the participle of 'iti' is suppletive — 'šel / šla', nothing like the infinitive; there is no regular form to build

lep_pozdrav.predictableError: it is the written (and phone) sign-off — walking out of a shop you say 'Nasvidenje', not 'Lep pozdrav'

hvala_za.predictableError: 'za' takes the ACCUSATIVE — 'Hvala za pomoč', 'Hvala za vabilo' — not the dative 'hvala pomoči' on the English 'thanks to' model

veselim_se.predictableError: the reflexive 'se' is obligatory and what follows goes GENITIVE — 'Veselim se srečanja'; and it is not 'Me veseli', which is 'nice to meet you'

hcerka.predictableError: 'hčerka' declines regularly — 'imam hčerko', 'dve hčerki' — while the standard 'hči' does not: its accusative is 'hčer' and its plural 'hčere'. It is not a diminutive; that is 'hčerkica'.

od_kod_si.predictableError: beginners build it off English and say 'Od kje si?' or 'Kje si od?'; the fixed phrase is 'od kod'

nisem_iz.predictableError: beginners split the negative into 'ne sem' on the English model; it's the one fused word 'nisem', and the country stays genitive after 'iz' — 'iz Slovenije', not 'iz Slovenija'

vikanje.gloss: vikanje — the polite 'vi': address ONE stranger with the plural verb ('Kako si?' → 'Kako ste?'; 'Kje živiš?' → 'Kje živite?')
vikanje.predictableError: using the ti-form with a stranger, an official or anyone older; the polite form is the PLURAL verb even for one person, and everything agreeing with it goes plural too — 'Ste bili?', not 'Ste bil?'
